chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: The New York Cotton Club and the Stormy Weather show
summary: He found the Harlem Cotton Club less glamorous than Sebastian's, and recalls Harold Arlen and Ethel Waters in the show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When was the first time you saw the Cotton Club -- when you went in there with the band -- that was when?
I think it was '33. Yes '33 -- the early part of '33.
Was that when you get back from Europe?

No, that was before we went to Europe -- I'm pretty sure. They went in there almost every year it seems -- for a certain number of weeks. But they had gone from the Cotton Club to the second trip in California. And then when they came back I came with them so it would have to
Uh-huh. What was it like playing the Cotton Club?

I wasn't too impressed with the Cotton Club because to me Sebastian's Cotton Club out in Los Angeles was much more glamorous. It wasn't as colloquial we'll say because they had these -- the Cotton Clubs looked like a bunch of cabins you know around a floor in New York.

They had tried to keep the idea of -- you know -- the Southern atmosphere. And the Cotton cabins and things around.

And in Los Angeles everything was just glamorous, stuff sticking to no certain motif.
WILLARD: But Sebastian undoubtedly named his club after the Cotton Club? (Portion of tape inaudible)
Oh yes, because at that time the word -- the name Cotton Club represented the highest in entertainment in the East so --
WILLARD: was the entertainment in keeping with the decor?
Yes, oh they had some terrific entertainers. And I think the first show in there when I went was the "Stormy Weather" show.
Now we're talking about New York.
In New York, yes. So there was Harold Arlen and Ethel Waters and all of those great stars. The show was really terrific. It was a terrific show.
